_readme: Server-specific death messages, in the same %1$s template form as
Minecraft's own en_us table so they compile into matchers identically.
%1$s is the victim. A template phrased '... by %2$s' also credits a killer;
that killer may be a mob, which the player_kills view filters out by
Templates are matched longest-first, so a precise one always beats a looser
one that would also match. Group keys are for humans only - every list is
To add one: paste the exact line the server sends, replace the player name
with %1$s (and any killer with %2$s), and add a case to the tests in
An entry is normally a string where %1$s is the victim. When a server puts
the killer first instead, use an object: {"template": ..., "killer": 1,
"victim": 2} to say which slot is which.
anarchyae: 💀 %1$s  drowned

anarchyae.note: Every death here is prefixed with 💀 and separated from the name by two spaces. The killer slot needs naming explicitly throughout: this server phrases it 'of %2$s', never 'by %2$s', so nothing can be inferred.
